# 4 Ezra Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Eagle vision interpreted

---

**12:1** And it came to pass while the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I saw —

**12:2** and behold! the remaining head disappeared. And the two wings that had gone over to it arose and set themselves up to reign, and their reign was short and full of uproar.

**12:3** And I saw, and behold: they also disappeared, and the whole body of the eagle was burned, and the earth was exceedingly terrified.

**12:4** Then I was awakened from the trance that held me as in a deep sleep; and great terror was upon me, and I said to my spirit:

**12:5** Behold, you have brought this upon me, in that you searched out the ways of the Most High!

**12:6** I am still weary in mind and very feeble in spirit; and there is not the least strength in me because of the great fear with which I was terrified this night.

**12:7** Now therefore I will beseech the Most High that he may strengthen me to the end.

**12:8** And I said: O LORD my God, if I have found favor in your sight, and if I am justified before you above many others, and if my prayer has indeed come before your face:

**12:9** strengthen me and show me your servant the interpretation and meaning of this fearful vision, that you may fully comfort my soul.

**12:10** For you have judged me worthy to be shown the end of the times and the last events of the ages.

**12:11** And he said to me: This is the interpretation of the vision which you saw:

**12:12** The eagle whom you saw come up from the sea is the fourth kingdom which appeared in a vision to your brother Daniel.

**12:13** But it was not expounded to him as I now expound it to you.

**12:14** Behold, the days come when there shall rise a kingdom on earth, and it shall be more terrible than all the kingdoms that were before it.

**12:15** And in it twelve kings shall reign, one after another.

**12:16** But the second that is to reign shall hold rule longer than any of the twelve.

**12:17** This is the interpretation of the twelve wings you saw.

**12:18** And whereas you heard a voice speaking not from its heads but from the midst of its body, this is the interpretation:

**12:19** There shall arise great contentions in the midst of it, and it shall be in danger of falling; nevertheless it shall not then fall, but shall be restored again to its original power.

**12:20** And whereas you saw eight small wings clinging to its wings, this is the interpretation:

**12:21** Eight kings shall arise in it, whose times shall be short and their years swift.

**12:22** And two of them shall perish when the middle time approaches; four shall be kept until the time when its end shall approach; but two shall be kept until the end itself.

**12:23** And whereas you saw three heads at rest, this is the interpretation:

**12:24** In its last days the Most High will raise up three kings, and they shall renew many things in it, and shall rule the earth

**12:25** and its inhabitants with much oppression — more than all those who were before them; therefore they are called the heads of the eagle.

**12:26** For these are they who shall bring his wickedness to completion and accomplish his last deeds.

**12:27** And whereas you saw the great middle head disappear — one of the kings shall die in his bed, yet in anguish.

**12:28** But the two that remain shall be slain by the sword.

**12:29** For the sword of one shall devour the other; but at the last he also shall fall by the sword.

**12:30** And whereas you saw the two small wings passing over to the head that was on the right side:

**12:31** This is the interpretation: these are they whom the Most High has kept unto the end — this is the small kingdom, full of trouble, as you saw.

**12:32** And the lion whom you saw rising out of the forest, roaring and speaking to the eagle, and reproving it for its unrighteousness, with all the words which you have heard —

**12:33** this is the Messiah whom the Most High has kept until the end of days, who shall spring from the seed of David, and who shall come and speak to them; he shall denounce them for their wickedness and the evil deeds they have done.

**12:34** For first he shall set them living before his judgment seat, and when he has reproved them he shall destroy them.

**12:35** But the rest of my people he shall deliver in mercy — those who have been preserved throughout my borders — and he shall make them joyful until the end comes, the day of judgment of which I spoke to you at the beginning.

**12:36** This is the dream which you saw, and this is its interpretation.

**12:37** And you alone were worthy to learn this secret of the Most High.

**12:38** Write therefore all these things which you have seen in a book, and put it in a hidden place.

**12:39** And you shall teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to comprehend and keep these secrets.

**12:40** But do not stay here yourself; go to a place where no mortal has dwelt.

**12:41** For you shall be taken up from among men, and from henceforth you shall dwell with my son and with those who are like you, until the times are ended.

**12:42** For the world has lost its youth, and the times begin to grow old.

**12:43** For the whole world has been divided into ten parts, and nine parts of it are already past and gone; and half of the tenth part is now passing away.

**12:44** Now therefore set your house in order, and reprove your people, and comfort the lowly among them, and instruct those who are wise.

**12:45** And now therefore renounce the life that is corruptible, and put away the thought of mortal life, and put away the burden of man, and put off now the weak nature.

**12:46** And lay aside the thoughts that are most grievous to you, and hasten to escape from these times.

**12:47** For evils greater than those which you have now seen shall be done hereafter; inasmuch as I have seen the kings of the nations becoming more powerful,

**12:48** and as their ungodliness increases, I and those who are like me shall be troubled.

**12:49** And it came to pass after three days that I sat under an oak, and no man was with me.

**12:50** For all the people had gathered to lament, because I had tarried so long; and I opened my mouth and began to speak to them.

**12:51** And I said: Hear me, O Israel! And give ear to my words, you seed of Jacob!
